items.title: A hacker built a tool to track police officers. Then he tried to warn them
items.description: A security flaw means the location of devices used by police, potentially including undercover officers and those travelling home, is visible to anyone with a phone or laptop.

items.title: A new poll tells us a lot about One Nation's new-found support
items.description: A new poll asks Australians specifically about One Nation and the results show that rather than being a flash in the pan, the minor party's freight train may be a more lasting phenomenon.

items.title: Tax windfall from Iran war to be pocketed in federal budget
items.description: The extra tax revenue generated by the Iran war will be saved in its entirety, as the government downplays major cost-of-living relief in next week's federal budget.

items.title: Iran daily briefing: Details on Iran's 14-point peace plan, and what else you should know now
items.description: Iran gives the US a 30-day deadline on its counteroffer for peace, which does not mention its nuclear ambitions.

items.title: Cargo ship in Strait of Hormuz says it was attacked as peace negotiations continue
items.description: A cargo ship near the Strait of Hormuz says it was attacked by multiple small craft, marking at least two dozen attacks in and around the strait since the Iran war began.

items.title: 'Friendships ended': Jewish Australians reveal impact of antisemitism
items.description: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion will hear from people with lived experience in public sessions beginning in Sydney this week.

items.title: Live: Japan's PM touches down in Canberra for first visit to Australia
items.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has touched down in Canberra for her first visit to Australia. Follow live.

items.title: We're headed into an AI fog as the automation arms race begins
items.description: Artificial intelligence might be driving growth for data centre companies, but society is unprepared for the long-term risks posed to the rest of us.

items.title: Australian businesses falling victim to new type of fraud
items.description: Higher inflation, a war in the Middle East, and a ban on surcharges are crippling small businesses. Now they are falling victim to a modern crime.

items.title: Russian woman's husband beat her but police were no help, so she wrote to Putin
items.description: Domestic violence and abuse have been described as an "epidemic" in multiple countries, but analysts argue there is something that sets Russia apart: the government is making things worse.

items.title: Interest rates and recession: What to know before tomorrow's RBA decision
items.description: Business journalist Emily Stewart walks you through the elements that will contribute to the RBA's decision to change the cash rate on Tuesday.

items.title: Police charge Jefferson Lewis, 47, with 5yo girl's murder
items.description: Northern Territory Police have charged Jefferson Lewis with the murder of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby in Alice Springs.

items.title: Tenants told 'breathing' contributes to mould in public housing
items.description: Despite unsafe and unusable bathrooms, cockroach infestations eating through wiring and constantly damp carpets, some Tasmanian public housing tenants are having to get the regulator to intervene in order to get solutions.

items.title: Contaminants are in your clothes, and brands don't need to tell you
items.description: Despite the rising flood of fast fashion coming into Australia, there's little regulation on hazardous substances in clothes.

items.title: What can you use your personal leave for?
items.description: People employed on a permanent basis in Australia are entitled to 10 days' paid personal leave a year. So what are the different types of personal leave and when can you use them?

items.title: Quiz: Can you name the typo on the $50 note?
items.description: Take a trip back in time with this week's history quiz.

items.title: Emerging Indigenous artists reveal their stories in major showcase
items.description: Revealed, Perth's long-running showcase of Aboriginal art from around Western Australia, allows budding artists to discover their creative side while strengthening their cultural bonds.

items.title: Australia's most remote communities losing essential services due to price of fuel
items.description: Cultural obligations and essential services are being impacted by the cost of fuel in Australia's most remote communities.

items.title: As fuel costs soar, cycling advocates argue our priorities are all wrong
items.description: Bike shops in Darwin are experiencing soaring demand as more people turn to one of the oldest and simplest alternatives to cars amid skyrocketing fuel prices, but advocates say the federal government is still prioritising drivers.

items.title: Piastri makes late charge for Miami GP podium as teen makes more F1 history
items.description: Oscar Piastri says the future is exciting for McLaren after the Australian made a late charge to finish third in the Formula 1 Miami Grand Prix.

items.title: The 'crazy idea' that became a world-first medical breakthrough
items.description: Travis Reyes survived a horror military aircraft crash but what came after was a two-year battle from doctors across Australia and the US to save his life.

items.title: Former bosses to face court over fatal mine collapse
items.description: Two former bosses are facing charges over a roof collapse at an underground mine in central Queensland in 2021 that killed a worker and seriously injured another.

items.title: High school girls use makeshift stretcher to rescue injured hiker
items.description: A group of high school students use a makeshift stretcher and put their Duke of Edinburgh Award training to the test while rescuing an injured hiker.

items.title: No to high-rise in our suburbs, new Victorian campaign group argues
items.description: Residents' groups across Victoria have formed an alliance ahead of the state election, calling for the community and councils to be given a voice when it comes to approving high-density housing.

items.title: A region promised a hospital by 2028 watches as cows graze on the site
items.description: Victoria's fast-growing West Gippsland region was promised a new hospital by 2028, but work has not started.
